$comment: Question sets for Jev on GTM container review. Shared set plus a web set and a server set. Written for this guide. Unrun against a live Jev endpoint.

intent_fit.instructions: Compare `change` with `request`. How well do the changes match what was asked?

consent_impact.instructions: Read `consent` and `change`. Does this change alter which tags may fire or which data may leave under each consent state?

criteria.possible: Might affect it; the state is not clear

name_fits_job.instructions: Do the names in `change` describe what each entity now does?

route_hint.instructions: Given `request`, `change`, `probes` and `flags`, should this be kept, sent for review, or reverted?

trigger_scope.instructions: Compare `web.trigger_probes[].after_matches` with `request`. Does a changed trigger fire on more or fewer pages than the request allows?

criteria.broader: Pages the request did not name

consent_default_sane.instructions: Read `web.consent_init`. Are default consent states set before any measurement tag could fire?

criteria.yes: Defaults are set and denied or region-scoped as the request implies
criteria.no: A tag could fire before defaults are set

server_hop_intent.instructions: Read `web.transport` and `request`. Does a changed tag send to the server container when the request did not ask for that?

criteria.unrequested: Sends to the server without being asked

claim_shift.instructions: Compare `server.claim_probes[].before_claimed_by` with `after_claimed_by`. Did a request move to a different client or become unclaimed?

criteria.none: Every probe is claimed by the same client
criteria.moved: At least one request is claimed by a different client
criteria.unclaimed: At least one request is now claimed by none

data_exposure.instructions: Compare `server.event_data_probes[].before_params` with `after_params`. Does any destination receive more user data classes than before?

criteria.more: More user data classes reach a destination

transformation_matches_request.instructions: Does each changed entry in `server.transformations` do what `request` describes, on the tags it names?

criteria.true: Kind, parameters and affected tags match the request

destination_complete.instructions: For each changed entry in `server.destinations`, does the tag have the fields the request names?

criteria.true: Nothing the request names is missing

hard_stops_in_code: consent.touched is true (route to review whatever Jev says)
server.event_data_probes[].user_data_classes_after gains a class on any destination
server.claim_probes has an after_claimed_by of null
server.destinations has a live_only tag in the change (Preview cannot observe it)

name_fits_job.instructions: Does the name of the entity in `change` describe what it does, judging from its type, parameters and notes?

scope_matches_name.instructions: Compare the entity name with `web.trigger_probes[].after_matches`. Does the trigger fire on fewer, the same, or more pages than its name says?

criteria.narrower: Fires on fewer pages than named
criteria.as_named: Fires on the pages its name says
criteria.broader: Fires on pages its name does not say

consent_fits_destination.instructions: Read `consent` and `server.destinations`. Do the tag's consent settings fit the vendor it sends to?

criteria.too_loose: Destination may receive data without matching consent
criteria.too_strict: Settings block more than the destination needs

purpose_documented.instructions: Do the notes on the entity say why it exists?

audit_rules: Jev answers may raise a finding to review. They never lower a code severity and never clear a hard stop.
